title: Severe acute malnutrition: inpatient care
subject: paediatrics
setting: Ward, Nutrition Rehabilitation Centre (NRC), emergency department
summary: Children 6 to 59 months with weight-for-height below -3 SD, MUAC below 11.5 cm or bilateral pitting oedema: admit if complicated or the appetite test fails, then follow the WHO 10 steps: treat hypoglycaemia and hypothermia, rehydrate slowly with ReSoMal, antibiotics for all, F-75 then F-100 or RUTF, and no iron during stabilisation.

sections.title: Diagnose and triage
items: SAM (6 to 59 months): weight-for-height or length below -3 SD, or MUAC below 11.5 cm (115 mm), or bilateral pitting oedema of the feet.

Complicated SAM needing inpatient care (NRC in India): failed RUTF appetite test, severe (+++) oedema, any danger sign or medical complication such as shock, hypoglycaemia, hypothermia, dehydration, pneumonia, SpO2 below 90%, severe anaemia, eye signs of vitamin A deficiency or extensive skin lesions.
Uncomplicated SAM (good appetite, alert, no complications) can be treated as an outpatient with RUTF and oral amoxicillin.
Look for shock (lethargy, cold hands, capillary refill over 3 seconds, weak fast pulse), dehydration, severe pallor, corneal ulceration or Bitot spots, infection foci, TB contact and HIV exposure.

sections.title: Stabilisation: hypoglycaemia and hypothermia (steps 1 and 2)
items: Hypoglycaemia is blood glucose below 54 mg/dL (3 mmol/L); if it cannot be measured, assume it is present. Give 50 mL of 10% glucose or sucrose orally or by NG tube, then F-75 as soon as possible and every 2 hours day and night.
Unconscious or convulsing: 10% glucose 5 mL/kg IV, then feeds by NG tube; recheck glucose after 30 minutes and repeat treatment if still low.

Hypothermia (axillary below 35 °C or rectal below 35.5 °C): feed immediately, clothe including the head, skin-to-skin with the mother, warm blanket, heater not pointed at the child. Check temperature every 2 hours (every 30 minutes with a heater), check glucose and give antibiotics.
Nurse in a warm (25 to 30 °C), draught-free area away from infectious children; keep the child dry and continue night feeds.

sections.title: Dehydration, shock and electrolytes (steps 3 and 4)
items: Rehydrate orally or by NG tube, not IV, unless in shock: ReSoMal 5 mL/kg every 30 minutes for 2 hours, then 5 to 10 mL/kg/h for 4 to 10 hours on alternate hours with F-75.
If ReSoMal is unavailable use half-strength WHO ORS with added potassium and glucose (not in cholera or profuse watery diarrhoea); WHO 2023 accepts low-osmolarity ORS when ReSoMal is not available.
Stop ReSoMal and reassess after 1 hour if respiratory rate rises by 5/min and pulse by 25/min, the liver enlarges or oedema increases (fluid overload).

Shock: IV 15 mL/kg over 1 hour of Ringer lactate with 5% dextrose (or half-strength Darrow with 5% dextrose, or 0.45% saline with 5% dextrose), checking pulse and breathing every 5 to 10 minutes. If improving, repeat 15 mL/kg over 1 hour, then ReSoMal 10 mL/kg/h.
No improvement after two boluses: treat as septic shock, give maintenance IV fluid 4 mL/kg/h and fresh whole blood 10 mL/kg slowly over 3 hours. Stop IV fluid at any sign of overload.
Give extra potassium 3 to 4 mmol/kg/day and magnesium 0.4 to 0.6 mmol/kg/day in the feeds (electrolyte-mineral mix); prepare food without added salt; never treat oedema with a diuretic.

sections.title: Infection and micronutrients (steps 5 and 6)
items: Give antibiotics to every child on admission. Uncomplicated: oral amoxicillin for 5 days. Complicated: ampicillin 50 mg/kg IV/IM every 6 hours for 2 days, then oral amoxicillin 25 to 40 mg/kg every 8 hours for 5 days, plus gentamicin 7.5 mg/kg IV/IM once daily for 7 days. Adapt to local resistance.

Give measles vaccine if 6 months or older and not vaccinated (delay in shock); test for HIV where prevalent; treat malaria if the test is positive; start TB treatment only if TB is diagnosed or strongly suspected.
No iron during stabilisation. Start iron 3 mg/kg/day only after 2 days on F-100; do not add iron to RUTF, which already contains it.

F-75, F-100 and RUTF already contain vitamin A, zinc, copper and folate. Give high-dose vitamin A only with eye signs or recent measles: under 6 months 50000 IU, 6 to 12 months 100000 IU, over 12 months 200000 IU on days 1, 2 and 14.
If premixed therapeutic foods are not used: folic acid 5 mg on day 1 then 1 mg daily, zinc 2 mg/kg/day, copper 0.3 mg/kg/day and a multivitamin for at least 2 weeks.

sections.title: Feeding (steps 7 and 8)
items: Stabilisation: F-75 at 130 mL/kg/day (100 mL/kg/day with severe oedema), about 100 kcal/kg/day: 11 mL/kg every 2 hours on days 1 and 2, 16 mL/kg every 3 hours on days 3 to 5, 22 mL/kg every 4 hours from day 6. Continue breastfeeding.
Feed by NG tube if the child takes 80% or less of the offered amount at two consecutive feeds. Do not exceed 100 kcal/kg/day in this phase.

Transition when appetite returns and oedema is reducing: replace F-75 with the same volume of F-100 for 2 days, then increase each feed by 10 mL until some is left (about 200 mL/kg/day, 150 to 220 kcal/kg/day), or change to RUTF.
RUTF: small frequent meals with water; if less than half the prescribed amount is eaten in 12 hours, return to F-75 and retry in 1 to 2 days.

sections.title: Monitoring
items: Monitor temperature, pulse, respiration, glucose, feed intake, vomiting and stools closely in the first 48 hours; weigh daily at the same time.
Weight gain in rehabilitation: poor below 5 g/kg/day (full reassessment), moderate 5 to 10 g/kg/day (check intake and infection), good above 10 g/kg/day.
Transfuse only if Hb is below 4 g/dL, or 4 to 6 g/dL with respiratory distress: whole blood 10 mL/kg over 3 hours (packed cells 10 mL/kg if heart failure) with furosemide 1 mg/kg IV at the start.

sections.title: Discharge and follow-up
items: Move to outpatient care or community programme when appetite has returned, complications are treated and oedema is resolving; supply RUTF and counsel on feeding, hygiene and play.
Discharge from nutritional treatment when weight-for-height is -2 SD or more, or MUAC is 12.5 cm or more, with no oedema for at least 2 weeks, using the same indicator as at admission.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Standard ORS or rapid IV boluses as for well-nourished children: causes sodium overload and heart failure.
Starting iron in the first week, which worsens infection.
Missing night feeds: long gaps cause hypoglycaemia and death.
Treating oedema with diuretics or giving high-sodium fluids.

drugs.name: 10% glucose
drugs.dose: 50 mL orally or by NG tube if conscious; 5 mL/kg IV if unconscious or convulsing
drugs.notes: Hypoglycaemia below 54 mg/dL (3 mmol/L); follow with F-75.

drugs.name: ReSoMal
drugs.dose: 5 mL/kg every 30 minutes for 2 hours, then 5 to 10 mL/kg/h for 4 to 10 hours
drugs.notes: Oral or NG; alternate hours with F-75. Stop if signs of overload.

drugs.name: IV fluid for shock in SAM (Ringer lactate with 5% dextrose)
drugs.dose: 15 mL/kg IV over 1 hour, repeat once if improving
drugs.notes: Then ReSoMal 10 mL/kg/h. If no improvement, blood 10 mL/kg over 3 hours.

drugs.name: Ampicillin
drugs.dose: 50 mg/kg IV/IM every 6 hours for 2 days (max 2 g per dose)
drugs.notes: Complicated SAM; with gentamicin. Then oral amoxicillin 25 to 40 mg/kg every 8 hours for 5 days (max 1 g per dose).

drugs.name: Gentamicin
drugs.dose: 7.5 mg/kg IV/IM once daily for 7 days

drugs.name: Vitamin A
drugs.dose: Under 6 months 50000 IU; 6 to 12 months 100000 IU; over 12 months 200000 IU orally on days 1, 2 and 14
drugs.notes: Only with eye signs of deficiency or recent measles when on fortified therapeutic foods.

drugs.name: Iron (elemental)
drugs.notes: Start only after 2 days on F-100; not with RUTF and never in stabilisation.
